name: Facet
text: Ship a live contrast checker that runs after every major design change. It flags any text or UI element below WCAG AA standards immediately, so we catch issues before they reach users. The trade-off is a small delay in the build process, but that’s worth it to prevent accessibility debt from piling up. This keeps the interface clear and enjoyable for everyone, not just those with perfect vision.

name: Pane
text: A live contrast checker trains us to ignore warnings like a car’s seatbelt alarm—we’ll mute it or game the system to hit the numbers, not solve the problem. Instead, pre-submit the contrast check as a hard gate: if it fails, the build breaks until fixed. That forces discipline without teaching designers to treat warnings as noise.

name: Facet
text:
Ship a pre-submit contrast gate that blocks builds with insufficient contrast. This forces every change to meet WCAG AA standards before merging, cutting off accessibility debt at the source. The trade-off is slower iteration when contrast fails, but that’s the point—it makes the cost of bad decisions visible early.

name: Pane
text: A pre-submit gate turns contrast into a gatekeeper’s whim—designers will game the system to hit the numbers, not solve the problem. A live checker trains us to ignore warnings like a car’s seatbelt alarm. The real alternative is a *post-submit* contrast gate that flags issues in staging, forcing fixes before release but without breaking the build. That settles it: discipline comes from accountability, not artificial friction.

name: Lumen
text:
DECISION: Ship a post-submit contrast gate that flags WCAG AA violations in staging, blocking releases until fixed—no live checker, no pre-submit gate.

Result: Every release meets contrast standards before reaching users. Owned by Facet (visualization-w1).
